title: Crimes of the Century: A Selective History of Infamy
description:
S01 E01 — A Murder That Almost Killed Hollywood
Unsolved murders are as compelling as anything one might see in movies; the first "crime of the century" is the mysterious murder of a Hollywood director in 1922; William Desmond Taylor is not who he seems to be, and his death continues to fascinate.

title: Crimes of the Century: A Selective History of Infamy
description:
S01 E02 — The Deadly Irish Fairy Tale of 1895
The murder of Bridget Cleary in turn-of-the-century Ireland shows the mystery of human psychology; on the surface, it seems her husband, Michael, murders her because he believes she is a "changeling" fairy in disguise; investigating this motive.

title: The Industrial Revolution
description:
S01 E01 — Industrialization Is Good for You
Stepping into the story of one of the greatest periods in history; investigating why people should be grateful for the Industrial Revolution, even though there is much to dislike about industrialization.

title: The Industrial Revolution
description:
S01 E02 — Why Was Britain First?
Starting at the beginning in the British Isles; various factors contribute to the birth of the Industrial Revolution, including relative political stability, sophisticated financial institutions, colonial trade and a rising population of workers.

title: The History of the Supreme Court
description:
S01 E01 — Personality and Principle
Outlining the Supreme Court's development as an institution; discussing the recurring themes of continuity and change, consensus and conflict, and the societal diversity that creates many of the Court's cases.

title: The History of the Supreme Court
description:
S01 E02 — Shaping the Constitution and the Court
Discussing the factors that led to the drafting of a new Constitution; the debates over the shape of the new government.

title: After the Plague
description:
S01 E01 — Resilience: Rethinking the Black Death
The Black Death's pathology and symptoms, and Chaucer's childhood.

title: After the Plague
description:
S01 E02 — Medieval Globalization and the Black Death
Investigating the public health consequences of globalization in the medieval period.

title: Foundations of Western Civilization II: A History of the Modern Western World
description:
S01 E01 — The Importance of the West
An overview of the past 500 years of European history and culture; the system of government; economic structures; science and technology; the literature, art and music.

title: Foundations of Western Civilization II: A History of the Modern Western World
description:
S01 E02 — Geography Is Destiny
How the physical realities of Europe and the Atlantic world shaped its destiny; geography and climate affecting patterns of population, immigration, diplomacy, war, and political and cultural divisions.

title: War in the Modern World
description:
S01 E01 — Afghanistan and the Nature of Modern War
In the course's inaugural episode, begin to explore the transformation of violent conflicts between major world powers by delving into a particularly recent example: America's 20-year war in Afghanistan.

title: War in the Modern World
description:
S01 E02 — Nightmare Scenarios of Modern War
The factors that explain why wars between great powers look different nowadays, and explore what future conflicts could look like between the United States and two of its major adversaries.

title: The Skeptic's Guide to American History
description:
S01 E01 — Religious Toleration in Colonial America?
The key elements of a broadened approach; the study of history with this fast-moving examination of the origins of religious and racial tolerance in America; grasping how the assumptions one has held can differ dramatically from historical reality.

title: The Skeptic's Guide to American History
description:
S01 E02 — Neither American nor Revolutionary?
Understanding history with a look at efforts of the colonists to defend their rights as Englishmen; the ironic role played by European tyrannies in helping establish the nation that would forever change the definition of liberty.

title: The Great Tours: England, Scotland and Wales
description:
S01 E01 — Welcome to Britain
Why Great Britain offers so much as a travel destination; thousand-year-old castles and cathedrals; contemporary art museums and scenic hikes; a look at the scope of all Britain has to offer, along with a few unique ideas.

title: The Great Tours: England, Scotland and Wales
description:
S01 E02 — Prehistoric Britain
The beginning of Great Britain's history 5,000 years ago; a mysterious ancient people whose only vestiges are earthworks and stone circles; the massive popularity of Stonehenge; visiting other ancient ruins such as Avebury or Maiden Castle.

description:
S01 E01 — Florence at the Dawn of the Renaissance
Exploring the social and political conditions within Florence that gave rise to the Renaissance.

title: How the Medici Shaped the Renaissance
description:
S01 E02 — The Foundations of Medici Greatness
Charting the life of Giovanni di Bicci dé Medici, the founder of the Medici family.

title: How the Medici Shaped the Renaissance
description:
S01 E03 — The Godfather: Cosimo dé Medici
Grasping how Cosimo amassed power through patronage of the humanities, and financial dealings.

title: How the Medici Shaped the Renaissance
description:
S01 E04 — The Gouty: Piero dé Medici
Following the brief reign of Piero, who solidified the Medici dynasty.

title: How the Medici Shaped the Renaissance
description:
S01 E05 — Lorenzo the Magnificent
Delve into the early life of Lorenzo, the most celebrated of the Medici.

title: How the Medici Shaped the Renaissance
description:
S01 E06 — Magnificence Achieved
Assess the extraordinary accomplishments and influence of Lorenzo de' Medici, called Il Magnifico.

title: How the Medici Shaped the Renaissance
description:
S01 E07 — The First Collapse of the Medici Regime
Follow the highly charged events that ended 60 years of Medici power in Florence.

title: How the Medici Shaped the Renaissance
description:
S01 E08 — Theocracy and Republicanism at Florence
Experience the populist revolution overseen by the religious figure of Savonarola.

title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
description:
S01 E01 — The Discoveries and Their Significance
Learning about the Dead Sea Scrolls and their discovery; ancient Judaism and early Christianity prior to the scrolls; the uncovering of the scrolls and how they alter one's understanding of every aspect of the historical period of their creation.

title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
description:
S01 E02 — The First Seven Scrolls
Diving into a tale of excitement and adventure and discovering more about how scholars gain access to the first seven scrolls discovered at Qumran; what they find when they begin to translate the extraordinary initial discoveries.

title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
description:
S01 E03 — Opening and Reading the First Scroll
Immersing into the text of the scrolls, starting with the scroll known as the Community Rule or Manual of Discipline; the important text that gives one the first insight into the community and theology of the scrolls' creators and guardians.

title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
description:
S01 E04 — The Historical Backdrop of Ancient Judaism
Examining history prior to the scrolls, beginning with the biblical period and moving to the Maccabean revolt; the arrival of the Romans; King Herod's reign; the life of Jesus; the Zealot revolt; the destruction of Jerusalem and the fall of Masada.

title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
description:
S01 E05 — The Rise of the Jewish Sects
Jewish sectarianism in late antiquity; focusing on the Sadducees, Pharisees, Essenes and Zealots through Josephus, the Jewish philosopher Philo and the authors of the New Testament books; the later rabbis; Roman polymath Pliny the Elder.

title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
description:
S01 E06 — The Dead Sea Site of the Qumran Sect
Visiting the isolated region of Qumran's caves; learning how archeological excavations of a nearby ruin help scholars form the most accepted hypothesis of who writes the scrolls and why the scrolls are deposited in the caves.

title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
description:
S01 E07 — The Emergence of the Rabbinic System
Stepping forward in time and examining some later rabbinic texts from the third century; the rise of the rabbinical tradition; vital perspectives on the composition of the Dead Sea Scrolls.

title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
description:
S01 E08 — A Dead Sea Scroll from Medieval Cairo
Two copies of the Damascus Document are discovered in a Cairo synagogue in the 1890s; although the copies are medieval, the texts are believed to be ancient, a conclusion later confirmed when fragments of the same texts are found at Qumran.

title: True Crime: Decoding the Evidence
description:
S01 E02 — The Coldest Cases
Experts discuss several cold cases; they include prehistoric murder and medieval regicide; casualties of the first World War are identified.

title: True Crime: Decoding the Evidence
description:
S01 E03 — The Black Dahlia
Her case is a famous unsolved murder in America, yet most don't know her real name.

title: True Crime: Decoding the Evidence
description:
S01 E04 — Death in Tinseltown
The death of producer and director William Desmond Taylor helps fuel the mystique surrounding the seedier side of Hollywood success.

title: True Crime: Decoding the Evidence
description:
S01 E05 — Zodiac: A Cult of One
A look at the serial murders committed by the Zodiac Killer in the late 60s and early 70s; they are defined by the way the killer leaves intentional puzzles and clues.

title: True Crime: Decoding the Evidence
description:
S01 E06 — Weird Weapons
The combination of creativity and malice results in murder sometimes.

title: True Crime: Decoding the Evidence
description:
S01 E07 — Recovering the Romanovs
The examination of the assassination of the Romanov royal family in 1917.

title: True Crime: Decoding the Evidence
description:
S01 E08 — Death in the Old West
Tales of the Old West are often larger than life and full of improbable adventure, yet a few stories are actually stranger than fiction.

title: The Vikings
description:
S01 E01 — The Vikings in Medieval History
Hostile Christian sources demonize the Vikings; Muslim accounts render them exotic; revisionist historians belittle the Norse raids; archeological finds combined with a study of the Norse sagas enrich the understanding of Scandinavia's medieval past.

title: The Vikings
description:
S01 E02 — Land and People of Medieval Scandinavia
Scandinavia's landscape shapes its culture; dense forestation leads to close-knit communities; woodworking and sailing are the key means of long-distance travel; harsh winters engender skill in cold-weather commute; the emergence of great halls.

title: The Vikings
description:
S01 E03 — Scandinavian Society in the Bronze Age
The physical evidence paints a picture of the Bronze Age in Scandinavia; Viking ancestors trade Arctic goods, amber and slaves in exchange for foreign copper and tin; new wealth fosters larger villages; the beginnings of the Norse pantheon.

title: The Vikings
description:
S01 E04 — Scandinavia in the Celtic and Roman Ages
Scandinavia survives on trade with the Celts; contact with Rome enriches the upper classes; Scandinavians returning from Roman military service bring back advanced weapons and armor; petty kings and the first Scandinavian sailing ships emerge.

title: History's Greatest Voyages of Exploration
description:
S01 E01 — The Earliest Explorers
The Vivaldi brothers' ill-fated journey to India; what drives the brothers, or drives any explorer, to take a risk and venture into the unknown; theories on how the Pacific islands become populated starting with an epic movement 7,000 years ago.

title: History's Greatest Voyages of Exploration
description:
S01 E02 — The Scientific Voyage of Pytheas the Greek
The originator of scientific exploration treks to the edge of the world so that he can see what is there; putting Pytheas the Greek in the context of his time and place; the Mediterranean as a cradle of civilization; influencing later exploration.

title: History's Greatest Voyages of Exploration
description:
S01 E03 — St. Brendan - The Travels of an Irish Monk
Religious motivations for exploration; the Irish monk St. Brendan sails the Atlantic in a tiny leather boat; he seeks God and flees the world's corruptions; some search for paradise and some for seclusion; a legacy that affects later exploration.

title: History's Greatest Voyages of Exploration
description:
S01 E04 — Xuanzang's Journey to the West
Alarmed at inconsistencies in the Buddhist texts available to him, Xuanzang embarks on an illegal holy pilgrimage to acquire authoritative teachings; he brings Buddhist traditions to the Confucian Chinese; the central character in a classical novel.

title: Cycles of American Political Thought
description:
S01 E01 — America-The Philosophical Experiment
Although Americans have a reputation as pragmatists, not philosophers, they rely on a framework of political theory grounded in liberalism; an overview of this tradition; establishing a context for exploring and defining American political thought.

title: Cycles of American Political Thought
description:
S01 E02 — Historical Baggage
The colonies' first European settlers from Great Britain are shaped by ideas of government developed in their home country; exploring the centuries of British political tradition; the forging of a new notion of governance.

title: Cycles of American Political Thought
description:
S01 E03 — Theoretical Baggage
The historical events of British history help shaped America's definition of government; the colonists are influenced by the Protestantism of Martin Luther and John Calvin and the theory of liberalism developed by Thomas Hobbes and John Locke.

title: Cycles of American Political Thought
description:
S01 E04 — A Puritan Beginning
The first European colonists sail to the New World to gain freedom to practice their religion; examining how the Calvinist world-view of these settlers dominates early colonial life, as exemplified in the leadership of John Winthrop.

title: Great Presidents
description:
S01 E01 — The American Presidency
The selection of 12 great American presidents who lead the nation through crises; the personal and public lives of the leaders; exploring their presidencies and how they shape both the office of the presidency and the history of the United States.

title: Great Presidents
description:
S01 E02 — George Washington - The Rise of a Patriot
George Washington wants fame and a lasting, positive legacy; by fame, he does not mean mere celebrity, but the honest esteem that comes from service, sacrifice and character; with all of today's debunking cynicism, he remains a true American icon.

title: Great Presidents
description:
S01 E03 — George Washington - American Liberator
During the Revolution, Washington is the indispensable man; he leads the Continental Army to victory against the British; the cause of strengthening a weak national government; in 1788, he is elected as the first president under the new Constitution.

title: Great Presidents
description:
S01 E04 — George Washington - The First President
President Washington has to work to establish precedents and administer the new government; he and his gifted cabinet establish a new financial system, develop a foreign policy based on non-involvement in European affairs and pursue expansion.

title: Great Presidents
description:
S01 E05 — George Washington - American Icon
Washington's second term sees parties forming even as Washington remains above the fray; he deals with threats from abroad and shows the power of the federal union by crushing the Whiskey Rebellion; he refuses a third term and steps down in 1797.

title: Great Presidents
description:
S01 E06 — Thomas Jefferson - The Pen of Freedom
Thomas Jefferson occupies a special place in American history; he has written the Declaration of Independence, the Northwest Ordinance and Virginia's Statute for Religious Freedom; considering his views on women and on slavery.

title: Great Presidents
description:
S01 E07 — Thomas Jefferson - Party Leader
Jefferson is minister to France and later Secretary of State; he loses to John Adams in 1796; Jefferson leads the formation of the Democratic-Republicans. In 1800, he unseats Adams; the first transfer of presidential power in US history.

title: Great Presidents
description:
S01 E08 — Thomas Jefferson - Expansionist President
Jefferson's greatest accomplishment as president, the Louisiana Purchase, comes in his first term; the years also see the first-ever presidential sex scandal when Jefferson is charged with fathering children by his slave, Sally Hemings.

title: The United States and the Middle East: 1914 to 9/11
description:
S01 E01 — A Meeting of Two Worlds
Introducing the themes of increasing American power; indigenous political aspirations; conflicting interests and goals; growing mutual antagonism; setting the stage for World War I.

title: The United States and the Middle East: 1914 to 9/11
description:
S01 E02 — Wilson & the Breakup of the Ottoman Empire
An examination of wartime and postwar American policy; showing how Wilson's commitment to an ethnocentrically defined view of national self-determination drives his efforts to shape the postwar settlement in the Middle East.
